reason: This passage from Numbers 22-24 depicts Yahweh's clear intention to protect and bless the Hebrew people (Israel). When Balak, king of Moab, seeks to hire Balaam to curse Israel out of fear of their strength, Yahweh: (1) initially forbids Balaam from cursing Israel, (2) sends an angel to oppose Balaam's journey, and (3) most importantly, compels Balaam to bless Israel repeatedly despite Balak's attempts to have them cursed from multiple locations. The blessings themselves affirm Israel's prosperity, military strength, and divine favor ('How goodly are thy tents, O Jacob'). Balaam explicitly acknowledges he cannot curse those whom God has blessed. The entire narrative structure demonstrates Yahweh's protective will toward Israel's wellbeing, even against external threats.
